markdown.markdown:
**SUMO (Simulation of Urban MObility)** is a microscopic and continuous multi-modal traffic 
simulation package designed to handle large networks.

[Docs](https://sumo.dlr.de/docs/index.html){target="_blank"}


SUMO is available to download on the [official website](https://eclipse.dev/sumo/){target="_blank"}. However, for the Traffic Analysis Zone (TAZ) part covered later in the workshop, we need to isntall SUMO with some extras. You may install SUMO with extras [here](https://sumo.dlr.de/releases/1.27.1/sumo-win64extra-1.27.1.msi).

During installation accept the defaults. Then check that it is installed by searching `sumo-gui`.

## Create `SUMO_HOME` system variable 

On Windows:

* Search for 'Edit the system environment variables'
* Click **Environment Variables**
* Create a new variable named `SUMO_HOME` in the 'System variables' section
* Enter the path to SUMO binary in the 'Variable value' text box. For example: `C:\Program Files (x86)\Eclipse\Sumo\`
* Click OK in all the windows

## Install `uv`

`uv` is "an extremely fast Python package and project manager". 

`uv` will help us installing Python and setting up a virtual environment with `traci` and other Python packages.

* Go to [Installation page](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/){target="_blank"}
* Run the command for your operating system, e.g., in Windows, copy and paste the given command in PowerShell (Open PowerShell by searching it in Windows).
* Close PowerShell


## Install Python

Python is needed for using TraCI (Traffic Control Interface). TraCI allows to retrieve values of simulated objects and to manipulate their behavior in a running simulation.

[Download and install Python manually](https://www.python.org/downloads/){target="_blank"}

Or see below to install Python via `uv` with the Positron IDE

## Install Positron IDE

Positron IDE is needed to:

* View or create simulation files
* Running TraCI with a specific virtual environment in Python

[Download and install Positron IDE](https://positron.posit.co/download.html){target="_blank"}

Accept all the defaults in the installation setup. Once installed, Positron would open by itself or you can open it by searching for `Positron`.

## Download and sync workshop folder

* Download the zipped folder [`sumo_workshop`](https://github.com/transportation-sci/sumo_workshop) from GitHub and extract it. You can download it by clicking the dropdown menu of the green code button and clicking `Download ZIP`. Make sure to extract it by right clicking the zipped folder and click Extract All.
* Open Positron, click Open > Open Folder and select the extracted folder
* You may see a dialog box in Positron asking if yoy trust the authors. Select yes I trust the authors. Dismiss any notifications.
* Run `uv sync` in terminal. If you don't see the terminal, click `Ctrl + Shift + backtick`. If the command `uv sync` does not work, restart Positron and try again.
* Once Python and packages are installed, you will see `.venv` created in Positron's files explorer. See if Python is working by clicking `Start Session` at the top-right of Positron and selecting `Python 3.14.x (uv: sumo-workshop)`. That would start Python in a console window (you may have to click allow in a different window first). Run the following Python command:

```python
1 + 1
```

If the code above runs, you're all set!
